text:
This looks like the end of 2013 or early 2014. Unemployment is 7.2%, which fits roughly September 2013. The 12m equity return of +27% fits late 2013, and gold is down 23% over 12m, which fits as well. The 10-year yield at 2.55% is lower than the 3%+ level of December 2013, so the date is probably earlier.

Checking the details: unemployment was 7.2% in September 2013 and 7.0% in November 2013. The 10-year yield was about 2.64% at the end of September 2013 and 2.75% at the end of October. The 3m change in unemployment is -0.4, and June 2013 was 7.5%, so that gives 7.1-7.2% around September or October. Headline CPI of 1.18% fits September 2013 (1.2%). The 3m change in the 10-year yield is -0.05, and the end of June 2013 was about 2.5%, so the end of September at about 2.6% fits. The 12m change of +0.83 also works, since September 2012 was about 1.65%.

US equities rose 3.9% in the month, which matches September 2013 (+3.1%) or October (+4.6%). Over 6 months the 10-year Treasury return of -4.3% fits September. Payrolls averaged about 143k, which fits the data as published then. The VIX at 13.65 is somewhat low for September 2013, when it closed around 16.6, but it fits October better, when it closed near 13.8. The October 2013 unemployment rate was 7.3%, though, and the CPI was 1.0%. The 10-year yield at end-October was 2.55%, which matches. The 3m change in the 10-year yield would then be from 2.60% at end-July, which gives -0.05. Fed funds at 0.08 also fits.

So October 2013 is the best fit.
